completed: Explicit export-movie command reuses authenticated retained MP4/MOV selection, original custody, current privacy screening and real native AVC/HEVC range owners.
All prerequisite coding spans must reach EOF; only unique selected luma is cached and exact selected presentation occurrences are exported, including repeated/backward edits.

One cumulative decode-work budget and one pre-I/O source-chunk read budget cover all spans. Separate limits bound metadata, aggregate coded samples, occurrences, luma cache, output bytes and MJPEG encode work.

PGM/MJPEG/gray-Matroska use existing private create-only output owners. Completion follows durable output; a selected unavailable RASL picture, cache/decode/source failure or empty selection creates no output.
Movie lineage binds original source pins, exact query/timescales/edits/gaps, selected occurrences and native receipt/pixel pins. No capture clock is rewritten.
Shared output-option parsing preserves existing frame/range output behavior. export-movie rejects trailing --manifest-out so a later write cannot follow its terminal completion marker.

cli_typecheck.resource_bounds: One job; debug0; incremental disabled; 6 GiB per-process virtual memory cap; pinned nightly; no injected compiler flags.

cli_typecheck.process_monitor_limit: /proc PID namespace mismatch; those observations discarded.

independent_review.finding_fixed: Rejected --manifest-out, including media destination aliases, to preserve terminal completion order.

important_boundaries: Original ADP-FILE-001 MP4/MOV imports only; reconstructed RTSP/catalog origins are not admitted by this selector.
Per-operation maximums are1024 coded samples and1024 output occurrences. Cached tight luma defaults64MiB/max256MiB; native frame/DPB/chunk memory has separate existing limits.
Full-original verification and native source-chunk read accounting are separate bounded phases. Native source reads default512MiB/max4GiB and do not renew at random-access boundaries.
PGM and gray-Matroska preserve screened luma; MJPEG is lossy. Gray-Matroska remains explicit uniform retiming, so source movie timing and gaps are metadata, not embedded playback timing.

Only completed export reports success; output-stage failures may leave a private incomplete file. No derivative publication, remote delivery, policy activation, UTC precision or physical-absence claim.
The synchronous command holds the existing exclusive deployment/publisher owner; supported competing writers cannot replace privacy authority during the operation.

No external or production dependency, gate or foreign runtime was added or weakened. The CLI native test oracle adds only an existing first-party fss-codec-h264 dev-dependency and corresponding lock edge.
